To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the optimal trade tax is positive; and (2) the effects of an increase in trade taxes on consumption and the capital-labor ratio are indeterminate.
an increase in the tax on exports (imports) raises the steady-state values (in the absence of a balanced-budget constraint) of consumption and the per-worker capital stock.

(i) increases in trade taxes lead to lower steady-state values of the consumption per worker, the capital stock per workers and the capital-output ratio, (ii) increases in the trade tax rates lead to lower steady state values of the consumption and the capital-output ratios and (iii) the optimal trade tax rate is zero.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of trade taxes on a small open economy which is not a price-taker in world markets, and where the consumer maximizes utility intertemporally.
the determination of the effects of increases of trade taxes on the level and rate of capital accumulation in an economy where the terms of trade are variable.
the effects of changes in trade taxes and the optimal trade tax in the context of an intertemporal model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the steady-state, increases in trade taxes lead to a reduction in consumption per worker and a reduction in the capital stock per capita, and that a tax on exports is preferable to a tax on imports.
, in general, increases in trade taxes will reduce the capital stock per person and the level of consumption per person.
trade taxes are not necessarily bad, that they can even be optimal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of trade taxes are not necessarily the same as in a two-sector, fixed terms of trade, price-taking consumer economy.
the effects of increases of trade taxes on the capital stock per laborer and on the steady-state consumption per laborer are ambiguous.
trade taxes are not necessarily welfare-reducing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the terms of trade are variable, the effects of trade taxes on consumption and the capital accumulation are not monotone.

, under the assumption that the elasticity of substitution is sufficiently high, an increase in the trade tax will lead to a reduction in the capital stock per capita, and a reduction in the consumption of the traded good per capita.
the effects of trade taxes depend on the elasticity of substitution between capital and labor.
